task.name: A document that policy requires a semantic review for is left unevaluated until an operator runs the evaluator by hand, so the gate withholds admission for work nothing has been scheduled to do
task.story_text:
Semantic readiness policy marks a typed document `required` once it reaches implementation
readiness, and a document with no evaluation record for its current revision is withheld
from admission. Nothing schedules that evaluation. The evaluator runs only when an operator
invokes it for one issue at a time, so the gate withholds work on the absence of a step no
part of the system has been asked to perform.

The effect is a state the intake contract does not intend: the document is structurally
runnable, policy declares a review necessary, and the only path forward is a keystroke per
issue. The milestone's own goal is capture → shaped → groomed → ready without operator
keystrokes, and this is the one transition that still demands them.

This is the sixth producer of the shape-gate router (#1450). The other five — diagnose,
groom, and their supporting slices — are filed. The semantic evaluator was not among them
because it did not exist when that epic was written.

Automatic invocation is a change to *what runs*, not to *what a result means*. A raised
finding still withholds admission until an operator ratifies it, and nothing here records a
ratification on the operator's behalf. Whether a clean evaluation can clear a document
without a per-issue operator decision is a separate question, governed by ADR-0009 clause 6,
and is deliberately not decided here.

## Acceptance criteria

- A document that policy marks as requiring a semantic review, and that has no evaluation
  record for its current revision, has one performed without an operator command. A document
  policy marks as not requiring one has no evaluation performed for it, and neither the
  presence nor absence of a record changes its admission.

- An evaluation is bound to the exact revision that occasioned it. A document whose revision
  changes does not carry a prior evaluation forward; the new revision reports as unevaluated
  until an evaluation runs against it.

- Automatic invocation changes only whether an evaluation happens. A raised finding withholds
  admission until an operator ratification is recorded against that revision, exactly as it
  does when the evaluator is invoked by hand, and no automatic path records a ratification.

- An evaluation that fails, times out, is refused, or cannot be attempted at all leaves the
  document reporting the failure and unevaluated. No failure mode leaves a document reading
  as evaluated-clean, and an unrecognised outcome is treated as a failure rather than mapped
  onto a known result.

- Invocation is bounded by the evidence it produces: a document is evaluated at most once per
  revision per prompt contract version, and a transition that recurs against an unchanged
  revision reuses the existing record rather than spending again.

- Operator invocation continues to work for any document, including one policy does not
  require a review for, and records its result on the same terms as an automatic one.

## Example

An enhancement is groomed until the structural gate returns runnable, which makes policy
require a semantic review of it. Today the ready queue withholds it as
`semantic_review_not_ratified` and stops; the operator discovers this by finding the issue
missing from the queue, then runs the evaluator and the ratification by hand.

With this in place, reaching that state performs the evaluation against that revision and
records it. Two outcomes follow:

```
no findings   → the record exists; admission still awaits the operator's ratification,
                which is one decision rather than two commands
findings      → the concerns are on record for that revision, and admission is withheld
                until the operator accepts or rejects them — unchanged from today
```

A subsequent edit to the body makes the recorded evaluation inapplicable, and the new
revision is evaluated in turn rather than inheriting the old result. An evaluation that
fails to parse leaves the document unevaluated with the failure recorded, and the document
is not admitted on the strength of a failure.

correspondences.description: An automatic semantic evaluation invoked from sprint query-mode admission or manifest resolution spends real agent budget before the sprint's cost ledger exists, so its cost is never advanced through SprintCostLedger and is invisible to the --budget cap.

When two documents have identical titles, bodies, and canonical types, reviewing the second automatically or manually reuses the first document's cache entry, appends another record under the first issue reference, and leaves the second document without usable evaluation evidence.

If an issue changes after semantic admission reads its revision but before sprint resolution fetches the task, the newly fetched revision is dispatched using the earlier revision's readiness without being evaluated.
When semantic audit records cannot be read, initial readiness derivation escapes the scheduler and both admission callers treat the required document as runnable without an evaluation.

When the evaluator cannot create its baseline or persist a failure record, automatic scheduling returns the document as generically unevaluated and does not report that the evaluation could not be attempted.
When the per-revision lock file cannot be opened, concurrent admissions both proceed without serialization and invoke the evaluator twice for the same issue, revision, and prompt contract.

When query-mode entry remediation turns a structurally skipped issue into a runnable required issue, the sprint re-adds it after the semantic scheduler has already run and the later dispatch check withholds it as unevaluated without creating any evaluation record.

When the semantic lock directory or file cannot be opened, admission leaves the required document as generically unevaluated with semantic_review_not_ratified and records no failure, even though the evaluation could not be attempted.
Query-mode --dry-run removes every required issue lacking a ratified semantic record before producing its dependency preview, so real fetched issues can be reported as no stories to run.
Automatic semantic evaluations incur recorded model cost before the sprint cost ledger exists, so the sprint total and --budget enforcement omit that spend.
When the dispatch guard removes a changed revision, the issue is not added to canonical skipped state or the terminal audit, and an all-removed run exits with only a no-stories message.

When semantic admission cannot read a remediated or manifest issue but the subsequent story fetch succeeds, the required revision receives no evaluation and is later withheld as ordinarily not ratified rather than as an evaluation that could not be attempted.

When the dispatch check withholds every query-mode story, the command returns before emitting an all-skipped audit, while manifest semantic withholdings are likewise discarded during resolution with only a warning.

Manifest resolution can run paid semantic evaluations before the sprint ledger exists, but unlike query mode it neither counts that cost against the budget nor prints the semantic-admission spend disclosure.

story_deviations: Automatic scheduling is stricter than AC5's literal bound: it invokes only when the revision has no successful record under ANY prompt contract version, not merely none under the active one. derive_semantic_readiness selects any successful record for the digest before considering failures and without contract identity, so scheduling a new contract over a ratified older success would let a fresh failure be masked by the stale success — the opposite of AC4's fail-closed requirement. Staying inside AC5's 'at most once' bound avoids that without changing admission semantics. Flagged in case reviewers want per-contract re-evaluation, which would require changing readiness derivation.

FrozenSemanticBaseline gained a `provenance` field (human/automatic) and freeze_baseline lets a human freeze supersede an automatically frozen EMPTY baseline. Not named in an AC, but without it the automatic path's empty freeze would permanently foreclose an operator's real baseline for that revision (freeze_baseline raises on any change) and would read as a zero-defect human baseline in golden-set calibration. Human baselines remain immutable.

ready_queue.py is left read-only by design (a status command must not spend), so an operator inspecting `forge status --ready` still sees a required-unevaluated issue as withheld until a sprint or manifest run schedules the evaluation. Status-time scheduling would be a separate story.

handoff.summary: Iteration 1 fixes all five P1 findings. (1) Content-cache identity: _cache_record now files a replayed outcome under the issue actually being reviewed rather than copying the cached issue_ref, so two content-identical documents each get usable evidence instead of the second being unevaluated forever; this fixes the manual path as well as the automatic one. (2) Revision handoff: GitHubIssueSource.fetch computes the semantic revision identity of the payload it built (over the raw body, before reopen context is appended) and records it on TaskStory as source_revision_digest/source_revision_type; a new semantic_dispatch_withholding() re-derives readiness against that identity, and both query-mode resolution (_withhold_stale_semantic_revisions in cli/sprint.py) and manifest issue entries withhold a story whose revision moved between admission and the fetch. This costs no gh call and validates exactly the payload the dev agent receives. derive_semantic_readiness was split so the digest-form derivation (derive_semantic_readiness_for_revision) is shared. (3) Unreadable audit storage no longer escapes the scheduler: every store read inside ensure_semantic_evaluation is answered as an evaluation_failed readiness that withholds, so neither admission caller's fail-open handler can admit a required document with no semantic state. (4) _record_cannot_attempt returns whether it persisted, and the scheduler reports the cannot-attempt failure from an in-memory failed readiness rather than a re-derivation, so a failure whose record could not be written still reports as failed rather than unevaluated. (5) A lock that cannot be opened or created now defers scheduling exactly like a lock held by a peer, instead of proceeding unserialized and breaking the once-per-revision-per-contract bound. Added 17 tests covering all of the above plus the reviewers' named coverage gaps (content twins on both paths, corrupt/unwritable storage through a production caller, lock-creation and lock-open failure, the baseline-frozen-in-between race, refused/timed-out/empty AgentResult variants, and the seam-level edit-between-admission-and-dispatch case). tests/conftest.py's existing _neutral_semantic_readiness_overlay fixture gained the new dispatch seam, on the same grounds as the three seams it already neutralizes.

The acceptance criterion permits at most one automatic evaluation per revision and prompt-contract version, irrespective of model. Changing the configured profile/model would therefore spend again for the same revision and contract.
  Suggestion: Give the automatic path a lookup keyed only by issue/revision and prompt-contract version, including successful and failed attempts. Keep the existing model-specific cache behavior for manual evaluation if required.
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Step 1 says to leave latest_successful_record admission semantics unchanged and re-derive readiness after the attempt. derive_semantic_readiness() in src/theforge/eval/semantic_readiness.py selects any successful record for the digest before considering failures, without prompt-contract identity. If an older contract succeeded and was ratified but the newly scheduled contract fails, readiness still returns reviewed_ready; the new failure is masked, contradicting the fail-closed criterion.
  Suggestion: Make readiness select the attempt applicable to the active automatic prompt contract, or otherwise ensure the newest applicable failed attempt takes precedence over stale success. Add a test with a ratified v1 success followed by a v2 failure.
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Step 1 proposes a lookup-then-invoke sequence, but SemanticReviewStore uses unlocked JSONL reads/appends. Concurrent query and manifest admissions can both observe no attempt and invoke the evaluator, so the stated at-most-once guarantee is not atomic.
  Suggestion: Serialize automatic scheduling with a per-identity lock or durable reservation covering the attempt check through evidence persistence, and test two concurrent scheduling calls.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Risk 2 (status surfaces and agent spend) is carried, not retired: Step 5 states the ready_queue outcome as an unresolved fork ('If ready_queue is changed to invoke the helper directly … otherwise leave it read-only'). The spec's own example frames the ready queue as where the operator discovers the withholding, so leaving it read-only means the evaluation is only scheduled when an operator starts a sprint or manifest run.
  Suggestion: Decide it in the plan rather than at implementation: keep ready_queue.py read-only (a status command must not spend), and make Step 5 comment/assertion work only — assert in tests that listing a required-unevaluated issue invokes no agent runner. If reviewers later want status-time scheduling, that is a separate story, not an in-flight fork.

  Suggestion: Add a new method (e.g. latest_attempt_for_identity) used only by the automatic helper and leave latest_record_for_identity untouched; add a test that a failed record still lets the manual command re-invoke the agent.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] The shape-gate seam is fail-open: any exception from derive_readiness is logged and readiness is set to None (shape_gate.py:574-578), after which the issue is appended to runnable. If the new automatic helper lets an exception escape — agent-launch wrapper error, store write failure, or freeze_baseline's ValueError when an existing baseline's defect_ids differ (semantic_storage.py:402-410) — a policy-required document is admitted with no semantic state at all, which is exactly the 'reads as clean on a failure' outcome AC4 forbids.
  Suggestion: Make the helper total: catch everything internally, append a STATUS_EVALUATION_FAILED record where a digest is computable, and always return a derived SemanticReadiness (STATE_EVALUATION_FAILED withholds via reason_code SEMANTIC_EVALUATION_FAILED_CODE). Changing the configured profile/model would therefore spend again for the same revision and contract.

Step 1 says to leave latest_successful_record admission semantics unchanged and re-derive readiness after the attempt. derive_semantic_readiness() in src/theforge/eval/semantic_readiness.py selects any successful record for the digest before considering failures, without prompt-contract identity. Step 1 proposes a lookup-then-invoke sequence, but SemanticReviewStore uses unlocked JSONL reads/appends. Concurrent query and manifest admissions can both observe no attempt and invoke the evaluator, so the stated at-most-once guarantee is not atomic.

The spec's own example frames the ready queue as where the operator discovers the withholding, so leaving it read-only means the evaluation is only scheduled when an operator starts a sprint or manifest run.

findings.description: AC5 bounds evaluation reuse by 'revision per prompt contract version,' but the Requirements section never introduces prompt contract versioning as a dimension of when re-evaluation is needed — only revision changes are discussed (paragraph 2 of Requirements, and AC2). This AC adds an unstated axis of invalidation with no requirement establishing what a prompt contract version is or why it should trigger re-evaluation.

finding_registry.description: An automatic semantic evaluation invoked from sprint query-mode admission or manifest resolution spends real agent budget before the sprint's cost ledger exists, so its cost is never advanced through SprintCostLedger and is invisible to the --budget cap.

When two documents have identical titles, bodies, and canonical types, reviewing the second automatically or manually reuses the first document's cache entry, appends another record under the first issue reference, and leaves the second document without usable evaluation evidence.

If an issue changes after semantic admission reads its revision but before sprint resolution fetches the task, the newly fetched revision is dispatched using the earlier revision's readiness without being evaluated.
When semantic audit records cannot be read, initial readiness derivation escapes the scheduler and both admission callers treat the required document as runnable without an evaluation.

When the evaluator cannot create its baseline or persist a failure record, automatic scheduling returns the document as generically unevaluated and does not report that the evaluation could not be attempted.
When the per-revision lock file cannot be opened, concurrent admissions both proceed without serialization and invoke the evaluator twice for the same issue, revision, and prompt contract.

When query-mode entry remediation turns a structurally skipped issue into a runnable required issue, the sprint re-adds it after the semantic scheduler has already run and the later dispatch check withholds it as unevaluated without creating any evaluation record.

When the semantic lock directory or file cannot be opened, admission leaves the required document as generically unevaluated with semantic_review_not_ratified and records no failure, even though the evaluation could not be attempted.
Query-mode --dry-run removes every required issue lacking a ratified semantic record before producing its dependency preview, so real fetched issues can be reported as no stories to run.
Automatic semantic evaluations incur recorded model cost before the sprint cost ledger exists, so the sprint total and --budget enforcement omit that spend.
When the dispatch guard removes a changed revision, the issue is not added to canonical skipped state or the terminal audit, and an all-removed run exits with only a no-stories message.

When semantic admission cannot read a remediated or manifest issue but the subsequent story fetch succeeds, the required revision receives no evaluation and is later withheld as ordinarily not ratified rather than as an evaluation that could not be attempted.

When the dispatch check withholds every query-mode story, the command returns before emitting an all-skipped audit, while manifest semantic withholdings are likewise discarded during resolution with only a warning.

Manifest resolution can run paid semantic evaluations before the sprint ledger exists, but unlike query mode it neither counts that cost against the budget nor prints the semantic-admission spend disclosure.

plan_structured.approach: Add a shared automatic semantic-review invocation path that runs only after structural admission says the current GitHub issue revision is implementation-ready and policy requires review. Reuse the existing evaluator, storage, prompt-contract identity, and ratification model so the change schedules missing evaluations without changing what semantic results mean.

steps.description: Add bounded automatic invocation around the existing semantic evaluator.
steps.details: Introduce an automatic-review helper in the semantic runner layer, reusing existing review_issue_semantically parameters for profile, secrets, prompt_contract_version, store, gh_issue_view, and agent_runner. The helper should derive the current SemanticReadiness first, do nothing when semantic_requirement is not required, skip live invocation when any prior attempt exists for the same input_digest, model_id, and prompt_contract_version, call review_issue_semantically for the missing-attempt case, and then re-derive readiness from the store. When no frozen baseline exists on the automatic path, pass an empty baseline_defect_ids tuple; when a baseline already exists, preserve it rather than freezing another one.

steps.details: Ensure the automatic helper records STATUS_EVALUATION_FAILED when invocation cannot be attempted before review_issue_semantically can append its own failure record, using the current title/body/labels-derived input_digest and the configured semantic model identity. criteria_mapping.criterion: A document that policy marks as requiring a semantic review, and that has no evaluation record for its current revision, has one performed without an operator command. A document policy marks as not requiring one has no evaluation performed for it, and neither the presence nor absence of a record changes its admission.

An evaluation is bound to the exact revision that occasioned it. A document whose revision changes does not carry a prior evaluation forward; the new revision reports as unevaluated until an evaluation runs against it.

Automatic invocation changes only whether an evaluation happens. A raised finding withholds admission until an operator ratification is recorded against that revision, exactly as it does when the evaluator is invoked by hand, and no automatic path records a ratification.

An evaluation that fails, times out, is refused, or cannot be attempted at all leaves the document reporting the failure and unevaluated. No failure mode leaves a document reading as evaluated-clean, and an unrecognised outcome is treated as a failure rather than mapped onto a known result.

Invocation is bounded by the evidence it produces: a document is evaluated at most once per revision per prompt contract version, and a transition that recurs against an unchanged revision reuses the existing record rather than spending again.
Operator invocation continues to work for any document, including one policy does not require a review for, and records its result on the same terms as an automatic one.
